_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics (Standard) 041, 2022 Term-II, series PPQQD/4 set 1. 12 pages, every one accounted for: idx 0 cover (bilingual); idx 1 Hindi General Instructions + Q1-4; idx 2 ENGLISH General Instructions + Q1-4; idx 3 Hindi Q5-8; idx 4 ENGLISH Q5-8; idx 5 Hindi Q9-11; idx 6 ENGLISH Q9-11; idx 7 Hindi Q12-13; idx 8 ENGLISH Q12-13 (Case Study - 1); idx 9 Hindi Q14; idx 10 ENGLISH Q14 (Case Study - 2); idx 11 blank apart from a '*' and the footer. English on the even indices 2-10. The top of every odd page was checked and opens with Hindi; no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion. STRUCTURE (General Instructions, idx 2): 14 questions, Sections A (Q1-6 @2), B (Q7-10 @3), C (Q11-14 @4, with two case study based questions) = 12 + 12 + 16 = 40, matching term2_m10 exactly. INTERNAL CHOICE: the instructions print counts, two in A, one in B, one in C = 4; found Q3, Q6, Q8, Q11, each printed (a) / OR / (b) and each confirmed against an 'Or' row in the marking scheme. The case studies (Q13, Q14) carry printed parts (a) and (b) of 2 marks each with no OR. 20 rows = 14 questions + 4 OR alternatives + 2 extra case-study parts. No MCQs, so no answer key. Decimal points on this paper are ordinary full stops (Q12 1.732, Q14 1.5). The marking scheme awards full credit to any attempt at Q13(b) ('even if deleted') and gives no solution for it. No reference papers in plan.txt: nothing skipped.

questions.subtopic: Mode of Grouped Data
questions.stem: The mode of a grouped frequency distribution is 75 and the modal class is 65-80. The frequency of the class preceding the modal class is 6 and the frequency of the class succeeding the modal class is 8. Find the frequency of the modal class.

questions.subtopic: nth Term of an AP
questions.stem: How many natural numbers are there between 1 and 1000 which are divisible by 5 but not by 2 ?

questions.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
questions.stem: If the sum of the roots of the quadratic equation \(ky^2 - 11y + (k - 23) = 0\) is \(\dfrac{13}{21}\) more than the product of the roots, then find the value of k.

questions.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
questions.stem: If \(x = -2\) is the common solution of quadratic equations \(ax^2 + x - 3a = 0\) and \(x^2 + bx + b = 0\), then find the value of \(a^2b\).

questions.subtopic: Median of Grouped Data
questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a silhouette photograph of a person in a yoga pose; every number is in the table. Page idx 8.
questions.context:
Yoga is an ancient practice which is a form of meditation and exercise. By practising yoga, we not even make our body healthy but also achieve inner peace and calmness. The International Yoga Day is celebrated on \(21^{\text{st}}\) of June every year since 2015.
To promote Yoga, Green park society in Pune organised a 7-day Yoga camp in their society. The number of people of different age groups who enrolled for this camp is given as follows :

| **Age Group** | 15 – 25 | 25 – 35 | 35 – 45 | 45 – 55 | 55 – 65 | 65 – 75 | 75 – 85 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Number of People** | 8 | 10 | 15 | 25 | 40 | 24 | 18 |

Based on the above, find the following :
questions.stem: Find the median age of people enrolled for the camp.

questions.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE - two photographs of Khurja pottery above a line drawing of the two shapes labelled I and II; the part names each object by its shape as well as its label, so it is answerable from the text. Page idx 10.
questions.context:
Khurja is a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh famous for the pottery. Khurja pottery is traditional Indian pottery work which has attracted Indians as well as foreigners with a variety of tea-sets, crockery and ceramic tile works. A huge portion of the ceramics used in the country is supplied by Khurja and is also referred as ‘The Ceramic Town’.
One of the private schools of Bulandshahr organised an Educational Tour for class 10 students to Khurja. Students were very excited about the trip. Following are the few pottery objects of Khurja.

Students found the shapes of the objects very interesting and they could easily relate them with mathematical shapes viz sphere, hemisphere, cylinder etc. Maths teacher who was accompanying the students asked following questions :
questions.stem: The internal radius of hemispherical bowl (filled completely with water) in I is 9 cm and radius and height of cylindrical jar in II is 1.5 cm and 4 cm respectively. If the hemispherical bowl is to be emptied in cylindrical jars, then how many cylindrical jars are required ?
